# Elliott Wave Analysis

⚠️ **Trading warning / Avertissement trading** : informational only, not investment advice. Elliott Wave counting is the most interpretive branch of technical analysis: two competent analysts can label the same chart differently, and any count can be invalidated by the next candle. Curated by Skill Harbor: an Elliott Wave workflow from the Weaxs stock-analysis-plugin, deliberately gated so it only runs when you explicitly ask for a wave count. It gathers 120 days of candles, then works through impulse structure first, enforcing the three rules that may not be broken (wave 2 never retraces past the start of wave 1, wave 3 is never the shortest impulse wave, wave 4 never enters wave 1 price territory), the character of each wave from the hesitant first to the divergent fifth, and the corrective patterns (zigzag, flat, triangle) that make up A-B-C corrections. Fibonacci relationships tie it together, the usual retracement and extension ratios for each wave against its neighbours. The output names the current wave position from the most recent clear starting point, the measurements behind the label, the most likely next path, and the price levels that would invalidate the count, which is the part that keeps the exercise honest. From the Weaxs/stock-analysis-plugin repository (MIT).
